adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent and deleteEvent the fallback logic is: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (undefined/null/""), the `.find()` predicate compares against that same falsy value, so it will not select the intended destination calendar (it will almost always return undefined). That makes `selectedCalendar/calendarId` undefined (or forces any later default like "primary"), so updates/deletes for events that were created in a non-primary destination calendar but have no stored `externalCalendarId` will be unable to target the correct calendar and can fail or act on the wrong calendar. This defect is directly visible in the diff.
